rules.title: Three-day Notice to Quit for disorderly, destructive or rule-violating conduct
rules.requirement: A landlord must give a three-day written Notice to Quit before evicting for causes described as disorderly, destructive, or violating written rules or lease provisions.
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies evicted for disorderly, destructive or rule/lease-violating causes under the Eviction Law.
rules.quoted_span: A three-day written Notice to Quit is required for any of the causes described as disorderly, destructive or violative of written rules or lease provisions (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2(a)).

rules.title: Rooming and boarding house evictions
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, unless the Bureau orders otherwise, and must give at least three (3) working days' notice to the County Welfare Board before starting an eviction action.
rules.key_value: at least three (3) working days' notice to the County Welfare Board
rules.coverage_text: Rooming and boarding houses: buildings with at least two living units occupied by unrelated persons without private kitchens and bathrooms, unless an exception in the Rooming and Boarding House Act applies.
rules.exemptions: Hotels with more than 85 percent temporary occupancy by people with homes elsewhere, school and college dormitories, buildings housing only college students and certain residences for the disabled; or if otherwise ordered by the Bureau.
rules.quoted_span: The Regulations Governing Rooming and Boarding Houses, which are enforced by the Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards of the Department of Community Affairs, require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau (N.J.A.C. 5:27-3.3(c)).

rules.title: Owner-occupancy eviction: occupancy requirement and penalty
rules.requirement: After a tenant vacates following notice that the landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit, the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months. If the landlord instead lets another tenant occupy it or registers a condominium or cooperative conversion, the landlord is liable to the former tenant for three (3) times the damages plus attorney fees and costs.
rules.key_value: at least six (6) months owner occupancy
rules.coverage_text: Units vacated after a notice that the landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit.
rules.penalty: Liability to the former tenant for three (3) times the damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs.
rules.quoted_span: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the  landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months.

rules.title: Removal from residential use: five-year bar and penalty
rules.requirement: After a tenant vacates following notice that the landlord will permanently board up, demolish or retire the building from residential use, the landlord must not use the property for residential use for five (5) years.
rules.coverage_text: Properties where a tenant vacated after notice that the building would be permanently boarded up, demolished or retired from residential use.
rules.penalty: Liability to the tenant for three (3) times the damages plus attorney fees and costs; civil penalty up to $10,000.00 for each violation; property may not be registered as a planned real estate development during the five-year period.
rules.quoted_span: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up or demolish the building or to permanently retire it from residential use, the landlord must not use this property for residential use for a period of five (5) years.

rules.title: Foreclosure: 90-day notice to quit for buyer occupancy
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction. Before evicting due to foreclosure, the landlord must give a 90-day notice to quit when the property was purchased by a buyer who wants to occupy it as a primary residence; a tenant with a lease extending beyond 90 days cannot be evicted until the lease expires.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenants of foreclosed properties purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy the property as a primary residence, including month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units.
rules.citation: Chase Manhattan Bank v. Josephson, 135 N.J. 209 (1994)
rules.quoted_span: Before a tenant can be evicted due to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t when the foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her primary residence.
rules.interaction_text: Month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units are not exempt from the 90-day notice requirements.

rules.title: Foreclosure Fairness Act notice to tenants after sale
rules.requirement: Any person acquiring a foreclosed property with residential rental units must notify tenants in English and Spanish within 10 business days after the sale that ownership has changed and that tenants are not required to move because of the foreclosure.
rules.key_value: within 10 business days after the sale
rules.coverage_text: Foreclosed properties containing one or more residential rental units.
rules.quoted_span: Any person acquiring a foreclosed property containing one or more residential rental units must provide notices to the tenants in English and Spanish, within 10 business days after the sale, letting tenants know that ownership has changed hands and that the tenants are not required to move because of the foreclosure.

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act
rules.requirement: Eligible senior citizens, permanently disabled tenants and certain disabled veterans in buildings converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership may be protected from eviction for 40 years if family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00, whichever is greater.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants at least 62 years of age before the conversion recording date, permanently disabled tenants, or certain honorably discharged veterans disabled at 60% or higher, living in a building being converted at least one year prior to the conversion recording date.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).
